His career in the boat trade has been accompanied by extensive ocean-going experience.

long_biography.plain_text:
Boatbuilder Sam Conor made the purchase price and condition of a hull central to Ocean Voyager's conversion work. He sought vessels less than a decade old with scope for substantial alteration. Strong resale demand for sound commercial boats made suitable starting prices difficult to obtain, while available capital constrained the size of projects.

His approach to interiors favoured straightforward, functional accommodation inside a workboat exterior. The aim was to give adventurous clients self-sufficient vessels for remote travel. One conversion supported remote fly-fishing, while others travelled to Easter Island and the Congo.
